conviction_note: Event confirmed by ST's own 5 Oct 2026 release (results before the European open on 29 Oct, call 09:30 CET). The move will turn on the formal Q4 guide against a ~$4.09bn consensus that already sits above the company's July 'above $4 billion'. The direct counterparties that have reported (NXP's Q4 guide +2% q/q, TI's Q4 flat at the midpoint) argue for a guide at or above that bar. Against them, this name has fallen on 7 of its last 9 results days, and the last four Q2/Q3 prints fell 14-18%. Those two cancel, so p_up is 50 and the scaled number is 0, while abs_move_pct is 10 on its own results-day distribution. The findings sum to +0.2 and do not disagree with that.

findings.finding: NXP, ST's closest direct peer in auto and industrial MCUs, reported Q3 revenue of $3.786bn after the US close on 27 Oct (+8% q/q). Automotive was +13% y/y and Industrial & IoT +39%, channel inventory was flat at 11 weeks, and it guided Q4 to $3.85bn at the midpoint (+2% q/q), above its usual Q4 seasonality. TI (21 Oct) guided Q4 $5.8-6.3bn, flat at the midpoint against Q3's $6.06bn. Both support ST printing a Q4 guide at or above the ~$4.09bn consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: ST's guide decides its prints. The Q2 2026 Q3 guide came in about 2.6% below the $3.80bn consensus and the stock fell 17.7% (23 Jul 2026). The Q1 2026 print with an upbeat Q2 guide rose 14.4% (23 Apr 2026). The Q3 2025 print fell 14.1% (23 Oct 2025).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. NXP released after the US close on 27 Oct, so 28 Oct is the first European session to trade it, and it sits inside the session that sets the window's opening close. By 14:30 UTC STMPA was -0.25% and NXPI -1.7% on its own print, so the market did not treat the peer guide as good news. Had it been fully read through to ST, STMPA would have outperformed the SOX on 28 Oct, and it did not. What stays unpriced is ST's own number against $4.09bn.
findings.independence: TI's Q4 guide, a separate document, points the same way: https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000097476/000009747626000165/q32026txnex99-eredgar.htm

findings.finding: ST's own results-day reactions, confirmed against its EDGAR results 6-K dates, are lopsided and large. Recent prints: -10.7% (30 Jan 2025), +5.3% (24 Apr 2025), -16.6% (24 Jul 2025), -14.1% (23 Oct 2025), -5.75% (29 Jan 2026), +14.4% (23 Apr 2026), -17.7% (23 Jul 2026). Over the last nine prints, 7 of 9 fell, including two Q2 prints (2024 and 2025) where revenue beat and the guide disappointed.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: This is the reaction history itself. Seven of nine results days were negative and the median absolute move is about 13%.
findings.why_not_priced: It is a reaction function, not a fact the price can absorb ahead of the print. The sealed baseline's history used estimated dates and put the median move at 3.85%. The confirmed results-day median is about three times that, so the scale has been understated rather than priced.
findings.independence: Press accounts of the July 2026 fall on a guide below consensus despite the beat: https://www.milanofinanza.it/news/stm-cade-17-7-sui-target-per-il-terzo-trimestre-2712101

baseline_tension: The baseline lean is +0.36, from the run-up term (20d -7.2%, 5d +3.5%), with no short anchor. The peer read-through agrees mildly with a positive lean and the reaction history cuts against it, so the net is roughly neutral and the evidence neither confirms nor fights the lean.
language_note: Italian rather than French sources carried the one company-sourced tone signal after July: the Equita note after the CFO's Citi presentation and a company contact. The English sources did not carry it.

The French sources (ABC Bourse, Fortuneo, Boursorama) carried only the results date and stale Q3 2025 items. On this well-covered dual-listed name they added nothing the English sources did not already carry.
lessons_applied: 'Let the reaction history move p_up, not abs_move_pct': the reaction-history finding went from -1.0 to -0.8 because its main weight belongs in p_up, and abs_move_pct stays at 10 rather than being capped
'A narrow proxy loses to a broad series / macro-to-company is a hypothesis': the Mercedes finding went from -0.2 to -0.1 because NXP's auto line, a direct counterparty, contradicts it
'The move is in the guide': confirmed that the Q4 guide line carries abs_move_pct at about the 9-10% guidance-event scale. No number changed
